title: Extended Mark resolved IR 2
description: The resolved IR (rir): what the xtmd compiler's checker understood of a build, written out. Every name is resolved to what it names, every value has its type, and nothing is lowered: prose is still Markdown, a call still has its arguments by name, and there are no bindings, sites or handlers. Every node keeps its span in its file's source and the comments that sit with it, so a tool can edit the source exactly or print it back. Renderers never read it: they run the IR (ir.schema.json). Types are the IR's. `xtmd compile --rir` writes it.

span.description: Where it is in its file's source: the byte offsets of its start and of its end, UTF-8.

comments.description: A node's comments, as written, `//` or `@//` included. `doc` holds its `//@` lines; `leading` the others on the lines just above it, with no blank line after them; `trailing` the comment that ends its line after its `;` or `,`; `block_start` and `block_end` the comments after an opening and a closing bracket (`{`, `(`, `[`) that end their lines, each with `at`, which of the node's own bracket pairs, counted from 0 in the order they are written (those of the nodes inside it aside); `free` the comments inside it after its last expression. On an expression, `free` holds the comments written just before it, inside the node it is in (`price + // before tax`, then `tax`).

id.description: A declaration's full name, `kit/chart`; a member's, `kit/chart.color`; a fn on a type, `kit/text.slug`. A surface's declarations are named by their version: `kit@1/chart`.

root.description: A build, resolved: the files given to the compiler, as its checker understood them.

rir.description: This format's version, a whole number of its own: a release may add parts; one that changes or removes a part, or what it means, raises it. The schemas of earlier versions are kept in schemas/rir-history.

xtmd.description: The Extended Mark release that wrote it: `0.3.1`.

levels.description: The levels the document needs to run (page 6), as its IR's top-level levels: none means its Markdown is enough. Only for a document.

pack.description: A pack in the build, and the surfaces of its earlier versions.

surface.description: A surface (`package kit@1;`): what an earlier version provided.

items.description: A pack it uses, at the version it uses.

file.description: One source file: a document, a pack's file or a surface.

package.description: A pack's file's package; left out for a document.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the source the spans are offsets into: a tool reads the source beside this file, and checks it is that one.

front_matter.description: A document's front matter: its text without the `---` lines, as the IR has it, and where it stands.

package_comments.description: The comments of a pack's file's package line.

head.description: Comment items above the package line.

import.description: `import kit;`, `import kit.chart;`, `import kit.chart as c;`, and what it brings in.

field.description: An input of a widget, a field of a record, a value of an extern block: its name, type and default.

param.description: A fn's parameter, or an event's.

generic.description: A type parameter and its bounds.

declaration.description: A declaration, with its id, its spans, its doc comments and its parts, every name in them resolved.

anyOf.description: A case, with the values it carries.

interface.description: An interface, or a widget interface.

widget.description: A widget written in Extended Mark.

piece.description: The piece of Markdown an extern is, from `markdown #quote;`.

extern_widget.description: A widget its renderer or its pack supplies.

oneOf.description: An extern fn; its body, when it has one, is its default.

extern.description: An extern block: values and fns the host supplies.

tokens.description: A tokens block: values for token cases.

migration_fn.description: A migration fn: a migration to reuse.

fn.description: A fn: its signature, every type resolved, and its body.

on.description: The type a fn is added to: a built-in's name (`text`), or a declaration's id.

signature.description: A fn's signature, with no body.

require.description: A `require` or a `warn` block: its message and its body.

var.description: A `let` or a `mut` in a widget or a fn.

expose.description: An `expose` block, answering an extern block.

migration.description: `migration kit@1 to kit@2 { … }`: its blocks, each naming the older version's declaration.

anyOf.description: A block: what happens to the uses of one older declaration.

migration_stmt.description: A statement of a migration's block.

call.description: A statement, `rename(to = plot)`, or a migration fn's call.

named.description: A named argument: of a widget's use (an input, or an event's handler), a record's field, or a migration statement.

use.description: A call of a widget, `@chart(values = v, color = color.OK) { … }`: the widget, and each argument, slot and handler by what it fills.

anyOf.description: A slot filled: by the call's children, or by name; in view code or in prose.

expr.description: An expression, every name resolved, with its type. Its kinds are the IR's, before lowering: no `bind`.

template.description: A text with holes: its pieces, and a hole between each two.

oneOf.description: `stat { label = "A" }`, or an inline record with no `of`.

case.description: An enum's or a token's case.

get.description: A read by name: what the name is.

call.description: A fn called by name, on a value or a type.

apply.description: A fn held in a value, called.

stmt.description: A statement of a fn's body, a handler or a view.

oneOf.description: A widget placed, in a view.
An expression as a statement: a call of an action.

block.description: A piece of prose, as the source has it: Markdown kept as written, between the calls and control lines that Extended Mark reads. A tool that wants paragraphs and headings reads the Markdown with any CommonMark reader.

oneOf.description: Lines of Markdown, up to the next call, control line or comment: paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, tables, code and maths blocks alike.
A call on a line of its own; the prose of its block is its slot's.

markdown.description: Markdown as written, each hole's place marked by U+FFFC, and the holes in order.

bracket_comment.description: A comment after a bracket that ends its line, and which of the node's bracket pairs it is.

comment_item.description: Comments on lines of their own that belong to no node: a run with a blank line after it, or one before a list's closing bracket. In a list they stand where they were written, like an entry; where a body's members are written in lists by kind, they are in its `comment_items`, placed by their span.

part_comment.description: The comments of a member written into its owner rather than as an entry of a list: a widget's `view`, `markdown`, `tokens` or `uses`, an extern block's `tokens`, a pack's `uses`, `provides` or `implements` line.
